html:
The Kaw, or Kansa, are a Native American people of the central Plains, who lived along the Kansas River in what is now northeastern Kansas. The river and the state are named after them.

They speak a Dhegiha Siouan language, shared with their kin the Osage, Omaha, Ponca and Quapaw, who by tradition all came west from the Ohio valley. The Kaw lived in earth lodge villages, farmed maize and went out on long bison hunts.

They traded with the French and later the Americans, while smallpox and the loss of hunting grounds shrank their numbers. Treaties cut their land again and again, and in 1873 they were moved to Oklahoma. Charles Curtis, vice president of the United States from 1929 to 1933, was a Kaw citizen. The tribe today is the Kaw Nation, based in Kaw City, Oklahoma.
